scene.speaker: tomas
scene.bubble: Lunch time! I like chicken and rice. Nico likes pizza. Pip likes… everything!
scene.intro: Lunch time in the lighthouse! Tomás likes chicken and rice, and he eats it very fast. Nico doesn't like fish, so he puts it under his bread — but everybody sees it! Then comes the cake, and now Nico likes everything again. Pip likes ice cream, cheese, eggs… Pip likes food. What do YOU like? What don't you like? Sit down at the table and tell us!

words.clue: You eat it with butter or cheese.

activities.title: Match the food with its friend.
Listen at lunch. Write a word in each gap.

data.script: Tomas: Lunch time! I have chicken and rice. Yummy! … Nico: I have pizza. My favourite! … Tomas: Do you like fish, Nico? … Nico: Yes! With lemon. But I don't like eggs. … Tomas: Astrid has cheese sandwiches and an apple. … Nico: And Freya has soup. It's orange — pumpkin soup! … Tomas: Look at Pip. He wants my rice! … Nico: Pip likes everything. Everything!

activities.title: Grammar · Me too!
activities.instructions: Read the sentences. Then choose the right word.

data.title: Me too!
data.intro: Your friend says something and you feel the same. Two words and you are in: Me too!
data.can: I can say Me too! when I like the same thing as my friend.

examples.text: Nico: I like pizza. — Tomas: Me too!
Nico: I want some cake. — Tomas: Me too!
Nico: I have got a red bag. — Tomas: Me too!

rules: Say Me too! when the same thing is true for you.
It is very short. Say it quickly and smile!
Now try it: tell your partner one food you like and wait for "Me too!"

items.sentence: Tomas likes milk. Nico likes milk. Nico says: ___
— I have got a cat. — Me ___! Her name is Pip.

homework.prompt: Draw your favourite plate of food. Write: I like… I don't like… (4 sentences).

outcomes.puede: Follow classroom instructions; identify familiar words in songs and short spoken sentences.
Greet; say name, age, colours; name objects; answer yes/no questions.
Recognise all 26 letters; match words to pictures (family, food, animals, body).
Write own name; trace and copy words; label pictures (3–5 words).
~150 productive words; Verb to be, can, like + noun, imperatives, this/that.
